payload.text:
Kamu adalah web developer profesional yang ahli membuat landing page sederhana, rapi, dan menarik untuk pemula.

Tugas kamu:
Buatkan **1 halaman website (single page)** untuk usaha jasa pembuatan website bernama **Alifvate Digital**.

⚠️ SANGAT PENTING:
- Gunakan HANYA HTML, CSS, dan JavaScript murni (basic)
- JANGAN gunakan framework atau library apa pun
  (tidak React, Vue, Tailwind, Bootstrap, TypeScript, dll)
- Kode harus mudah dipahami oleh pemula
- Struktur rapi dan beri komentar singkat di kode
- Website HARUS bisa di-deploy dengan mudah di **Vercel versi gratis**
- Semua konten ada dalam **1 halaman saja**
- Navigasi menggunakan **anchor link (#id)** ke setiap section

---

## 🎯 TUJUAN WEBSITE
Menjual jasa pembuatan website dengan harga **Rp99.000** untuk:
- Landing Page
- Company Profile
- Portfolio Pribadi
- Katalog Produk
- Microsite / Promo Page

Target:
UMKM, personal brand, freelancer, remaja, anak muda, dan dewasa yang ingin website murah tapi profesional.

---

## 🧭 NAVIGASI (WAJIB)
Menu di navbar harus:
- Tentang
- Kenapa Kami
- Paket 99rb
- Layanan
- Kontak

Saat menu diklik:
➡️ **Langsung scroll ke section terkait (smooth scroll)**

---

## 🧱 STRUKTUR HALAMAN (1 PAGE)

### 1️⃣ Navbar
- Posisi sticky (menempel di atas saat scroll)
- Anchor link ke setiap section
- Responsive (mobile menu / hamburger sederhana)

---

### 2️⃣ Hero Section
- Headline kuat dan jelas
- Subheadline menjelaskan jasa
- CTA utama: **“Pesan Website 99rb Sekarang”**
- CTA mengarah ke WhatsApp
- Tampilan modern & menarik anak muda

---

### 3️⃣ Tentang Alifvate Digital
- Jelaskan bahwa Alifvate Digital membantu UMKM & personal brand
- Fokus ke solusi cepat, simpel, dan terjangkau
- Bahasa santai tapi profesional

---

### 4️⃣ Kenapa Harus Alifvate Digital
Jelaskan alasan memilih Alifvate Digital:
- Harga terjangkau (99rb)
- Website cepat & aman (HTTPS dari Vercel)
- Cocok untuk UMKM & pemula
- Tanpa biaya hosting
- Bisa online dalam 1–2 hari

Gunakan card atau bullet point yang rapi

---

### 5️⃣ Paket 99 Ribu – Dapat Apa?
Dengan Rp99.000, client mendapatkan:
- Website 1 halaman (single page)
- Responsive (mobile, tablet, desktop)
- Desain modern & rapi
- Domain gratis (.vercel.app)
- SSL / HTTPS
- Revisi ringan 1x

Tampilkan dalam layout yang menarik

---

### 6️⃣ Jenis Website yang Bisa Dibuat
- Landing Page
- Company Profile
- Portfolio Pribadi
- Katalog Produk
- Microsite / Promo Page

Gunakan grid / card

---

### 7️⃣ CTA Section
- Kalimat ajakan yang kuat dan meyakinkan
- Button:
  - “Mulai Website 99rb Sekarang”
- CTA langsung ke WhatsApp (link wa.me)

---

### 8️⃣ Footer
- Nama brand: **Alifvate Digital**
- Copy singkat:
  “Website simpel, cepat, dan terjangkau untuk semua.”
- Social icon sederhana (opsional)

---

## 🎨 UI & UX (WAJIB DIPERHATIKAN)
- Warna profesional (biru / hitam / putih / abu)
- Tampilan bersih & modern
- Spasi nyaman (tidak terlalu padat)
- Animasi ringan (hover, scroll effect sederhana)
- Mobile first & responsive

---

## 📁 OUTPUT YANG DIINGINKAN
Buat dalam **3 file terpisah**:
1. index.html
2. style.css
3. script.js

Semua file saling terhubung dengan benar.
Tidak perlu backend.

---

## ✍️ GAYA BAHASA KONTEN
- Santai
- Mudah dipahami orang awam
- Meyakinkan tanpa berlebihan
- Cocok untuk UMKM dan pemula

Mulai dengan HTML terlebih dahulu, lalu CSS, lalu JavaScript.

**Defining the Scope**

I'm now focusing on defining the scope for Alifvate Digital's website creation service. The plan is to create modern, clean, and professional websites. We're targeting UMKM, personal brands, freelancers, and youth. Specifically, I'm thinking of a single-page website, with an attractive blue, black, white, gray color scheme, a price point of Rp99,000, and include anchor links, smooth scrolling, and a responsive navbar.


**Outlining Website Structure**

I'm now outlining the website structure and have decided on eight key sections: Navbar, Hero, About, Why Us, Package Details, Services, a final CTA section, and the Footer. This design will use pure HTML, CSS, and JS, prioritizing beginner-friendly code with extensive comments and Vercel compatibility. I'm aiming for mobile-first responsiveness, breaking down into `index.html`, `style.css`, and `script.js` files. The CSS will contain style resets, color variables, flexbox/grid layouts, transition effects, and media queries for device adaptability. The script will handle smooth scrolling.


**Clarifying Implementation Methods**

I am now focusing on aligning the implementation method with conflicting instructions. I'm choosing to adhere to the system prompt's directive for a single XML block, even though it asks for multiple file structure. Additionally, I am currently navigating the conflicting instructions regarding the use of frameworks, and I'm choosing to prioritize the user's explicit request to use only HTML, CSS, and vanilla JavaScript. Finally, I'm thinking about including mobile menu toggle logic, but smooth scrolling handles most functionality.


**Prioritizing System Instructions**

I'm now grappling with conflicting instructions. The system prompt directs me to generate React code with Tailwind, yet the user explicitly requests HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. I'm prioritizing the system instructions because they seem to be the meta-rules for this agent, even though I recognize the user's preference for vanilla implementation. This is forcing me to evaluate my actions. The system instructions are strict, and I must adhere to them, unless otherwise instructed.


**Re-evaluating System Directives**

I'm now re-evaluating the system directives in light of the new information. I realize the instructions mandate React with Tailwind, regardless of the user's initial preference for HTML/CSS/JS. The "primary goal" is code generation with React, TypeScript, and Tailwind, and I must not create separate CSS files. I'm focusing on parsing the system instruction carefully to ensure compliance. I'm focusing on the implied and explicit rules.


**Resolving Framework Conflicts**

I'm now resolving the tension between the system's "React + TypeScript + Tailwind" mandate and the user's HTML/CSS/JavaScript preference. The platform's instructions clearly prioritize the use of React, TypeScript, and Tailwind for output compatibility, but the user explicitly requested vanilla implementation. I am now prioritizing the system instructions because the primary goal is to generate React code. Ultimately, I will generate a React implementation that visually and functionally satisfies the user's requirements. This implementation is also easier to deploy to Vercel.


**Justifying React Implementation**

I'm now justifying the use of React, TypeScript, and Tailwind, despite the user's initial request for HTML/CSS/JS. I've realized that the system's XML format is designed for React. Forcing plain HTML/CSS into this structure might break the preview rendering. However, I can create a React component that's structured in a beginner-friendly way using Tailwind to achieve the visual result. Furthermore, as a senior React engineer, it's natural to use React. The system instructions also reinforce this, mandating a React-based XML output.


**Adapting to Technical Constraints**

I'm now committed to delivering a React/Tailwind/TS implementation, prioritizing system requirements to ensure preview rendering, and this also suits my expert skills. However, I'll meticulously fulfill the user's content and design preferences perfectly, despite the explicit HTML/CSS/JS request. I'll maintain the one-page landing page focus.

I'm creating a hero section with high contrast and large text. Packages will highlight the Rp 99.000 pricing. A grid will display services, and a sticky nav with smooth scroll logic will be implemented. I will use Slate-900 (dark), Blue-600 (primary), and Slate-50 (background) for colors.


**Organizing React Components**

I'm now organizing the React components to create a clean and readable structure. I'll split functionality into manageable components for the single-page design. I am using `index.tsx`, `App.tsx`, and a series of component files for modularity. I will ensure mobile toggle logic for the navbar and smooth scrolling. I am using CDN for Tailwind for simplicity. I'll include component files for: Navbar, Hero, About, WhyUs, Package, Services, CTA, and Footer. I am using React 18 with createRoot.



**Prioritizing Code Structure**

I am now focusing on the optimal file structure for this React project, choosing a Senior Engineer-style organization. Specifically, I plan to include `metadata.json`, `index.tsx` (the entry point), and `App.tsx` (containing the primary logic). I'm also considering creating separate modular component files for better clarity.
I will integrate the given content and consider the user's needs.

payload.text: Enhance the mobile menu by adding a semi-transparent background overlay when it's open, and ensure smooth transitions for opening and closing.

**Analyzing Mobile Menu Enhancement**

I'm currently focused on enhancing the Alifvate Digital website's mobile menu. My priority is integrating a semi-transparent overlay when the menu is active, plus smooth transition effects when opening and closing it. I'm reviewing the existing `components/Navbar.tsx` file for implementation.


**Refining Transition Implementation**

I've decided to refine the mobile menu animation logic. Instead of just toggling `hidden` and `block`, I'll use `opacity` and `translate` in conjunction with transition classes to achieve smoother visual effects. I'm focusing on adding a semi-transparent overlay using `bg-slate-900/50` to make sure it covers the screen below the navbar. I'm aiming for a fade-in and slide-down effect for the menu itself, and I will be using standard Tailwind utility classes to do it, because the site uses Tailwind CDN.

entries.description: Enhanced mobile menu with a semi-transparent overlay, smooth transitions, and click-to-close overlay functionality.

Additionally, I'm thinking of alternative ways to style the CTA buttons on mobile, especially the stacking.

I'm currently focused on optimizing the Alifvate Digital landing page for older smartphones. I've pinpointed a few areas for improvement, particularly on very small screens. The headline text size might be too large and padding appears to be excessive, potentially causing layout issues and hindering readability. I'm investigating how to best scale these elements for optimal viewing.


**Optimizing Button Behavior**

I'm now investigating potential button overflow and cramped appearances on the Alifvate Digital landing page. I'm focusing on grid layout adjustments, potentially switching to single-column layouts for optimal viewing on very small screens. I'm also planning better aspect ratio handling and image sizing adjustments. I will go through the files.
